words.root_logic: capere（抓取）经古北法语 cachier（追捕）→ 伸手把动着的东西拿住
words.origin: 古北法语 cachier（追、捕）← 通俗拉丁语 captiare ← 拉丁语 capere（抓取）
words.native_definition: to take hold of something moving; to be in time for
words.core_concept: closing the hand on something already in motion – 把正动着的东西一把攥住
words.core_image: 球还在半空，他一伸手扣住了
examples: She caught the ball with one hand.
He just caught the last train.
semantic_expansions: 抓住：把动着的东西一把攥住
赶上：在开走之前把它抓着
染上：病像被抓住一样落到身上
words.recall_hint: capere（抓取）→ 把正动着的东西一把攥住

words.root_logic: capere（抓取）经古法语 chacier（追猎）→ 一路追着要抓住
words.origin: 古法语 chacier（追猎）← 通俗拉丁语 captiare ← 拉丁语 capere；与 catch 同源分支
words.native_definition: to run after someone or something to catch them
words.core_concept: keeping after a thing because the hand has not closed on it yet – 手还没抓住，脚就一直跟着
words.core_image: 狗撒开腿跟着那团影子跑，隔一段又追近些
examples: The dog chased the rabbit.
Police chased the car for miles.
semantic_expansions: 追赶/追捕：手未及、脚先跟着不放
追求：同一个追法用在人或目标上
words.recall_hint: capere（抓取）→ 手未及先追着，chacier 一支

words.root_logic: cadere（落下）→ 骰子落地那一面 → 碰巧、机会
words.origin: 古法语 cheance（掷骰所得）← 通俗拉丁语 cadentia（落下之势）← 拉丁语 cadere（落下）
words.native_definition: a possibility of something happening; an opportunity
words.core_concept: which face the die shows when it stops rolling – 骰子停下来时朝上的那一面
words.core_image: 骰子在桌上滚了两圈，停下时朝上那面谁也没料到
examples: This is your last chance.
There is a chance of rain today.
semantic_expansions: 机会：骰子恰好落成对你有利那面
可能性：它可能落成的各面之一
偶然：落成哪面并非人定
words.recall_hint: cadere（落下）→ 骰子停下时朝上那一面

words.root_logic: cadere（落下）→ escheat（无主财产归公）→ 借职权占人便宜 → 欺骗
words.origin: 中古英语 cheten，截自 escheat（封建法中无嗣田产落归领主）← 古法语 eschete ← cadere（落下）
words.native_definition: to act dishonestly to gain an advantage
words.core_concept: taking what fell to another and calling it one's own – 把该落到别人手里的据为己有
words.core_image: 他把牌往袖口一带，抬头时脸上没有半点异样
examples: He cheated in the exam.
She felt cheated by the deal.
semantic_expansions: 欺骗/作弊：把该落给别人的悄悄占去
骗子：惯做此事的那个人
words.recall_hint: cadere（落下）→ 把落归他人之物占去

words.root_logic: civis（市民）→ civitas（市民共同体）→ 市民聚居之地
words.origin: 古法语 cité ← 拉丁语 civitas（公民共同体、城邦）← civis（市民）
words.native_definition: a large town where many people live and work
words.core_concept: the place named after the body of people in it, not its walls – 以住在里头的人得名，而非以城墙
words.core_image: 屋顶一直连到天边，路口的人流从早到晚没断过
examples: She moved to the city last year.
The city has three million people.
semantic_expansions: 城市/都市：以聚居其中的市民得名的那处地方
words.recall_hint: civis（市民）→ civitas（市民共同体）→ 其聚居之地

words.root_logic: civis（市民）+ -zen（居者）→ 属这座城、有其权利与义务的人
words.origin: 盎格鲁法语 citezein ← 古法语 citeain ← 拉丁语 civitas ← civis（市民）
words.native_definition: a person who legally belongs to a country and has its rights
words.core_concept: the one the city counts as its own – 被这座城认作自己人的那个
words.core_image: 他掏出那本册子，柜台后的人点点头就放行了
examples: Every citizen may vote.
She became a citizen last spring.
semantic_expansions: 公民：被国家认作自己人、有权利义务的那个
市民/居民：同理，落在城这一级
words.recall_hint: civis（市民）+ -zen（居者）→ 被这座城认作自己人的

words.root_logic: habere（拿住）→ habilis（好操持的）→ 拿得住、使得动 → 有能力的
words.origin: 古法语 able ← 拉丁语 habilis（易于操持的）← habere（拿住）
words.native_definition: having the skill or power to do something
words.core_concept: the hand that can actually hold and work the thing – 手真拿得住、使得动的那种
words.core_image: 别人拧不开那个盖子，递给他一转就开了
examples: She is able to speak three languages.
He was not able to come.
semantic_expansions: 能够的/有能力的：手真拿得住、使得动的那种
words.recall_hint: habere（拿住）→ habilis（好操持）→ 拿得住

words.root_logic: able（拿得住）+ -ity → 拿得住这件事本身 → 能力
words.origin: 古法语 ablete ← 拉丁语 habilitas（易操持的性质）← habere（拿住）
words.native_definition: the power or skill needed to do something
words.core_concept: how much the hand can actually take on – 那双手到底拿得住多少
words.core_image: 同一副担子有人挑不起，有人挑起来还能走
examples: She has great ability in maths.
It is beyond my ability to fix.
semantic_expansions: 能力/才能：手拿得住、使得动的那份分量
words.recall_hint: able（拿得住）+ -ity → 拿得住的那份分量

words.root_logic: al-（ad- 朝）+ lig（绑）→ 绑到一处的那一方 → 盟友
words.origin: 古法语 alier（结合）← 拉丁语 alligare（捆在一起）← ad＋ligare（绑）
words.native_definition: a country or person joined with another for a shared purpose
words.core_concept: the one tied to your side by the same cord – 被同一根绳系到你这边的那方
words.core_image: 两只手腕被一根绳系住，往哪走都得一块儿
examples: Britain was a wartime ally.
The two nations allied against the threat.
semantic_expansions: 盟友/同盟者：被同一根绳系到自己这边的那方
结盟：把两方系到一处这个动作
words.recall_hint: al-（朝）+ lig（绑）→ 被同一根绳系到一处

words.root_logic: ally（结盟）+ -ance → 系在一处这件事，及系成的那个组合
words.origin: 古法语 aliance（结盟）← alier ← 拉丁语 alligare ← ad＋ligare（绑）
words.native_definition: a formal agreement between countries or groups to work together
words.core_concept: the knot itself, once two sides are corded together – 两方系妥之后那个结
words.core_image: 绳头交叉压紧，打成一个谁也抽不开的结
examples: The alliance lasted thirty years.
They formed an alliance in 1949.
semantic_expansions: 联盟/同盟：两方系妥之后成的那个结
结盟：打这个结的过程
words.recall_hint: ally（结盟）+ -ance → 两方系妥后成的那个结

words.root_logic: al-（ad- 朝）+ loy（绑）→ 两种金属绑成一体 → 合金
words.origin: 古法语 aloi（成色）← aloier（混合）← 拉丁语 alligare（捆在一起）← ad＋ligare
words.native_definition: a metal made by melting two or more metals together
words.core_concept: two metals corded into one body that no longer comes apart – 两种金属绑成一体，再分不开
words.core_image: 炉里两样金属化在一处，冷了以后倒不出哪是哪
examples: Brass is an alloy of copper and zinc.
The frame is made of light alloy.
semantic_expansions: 合金：两种金属绑成一体、再分不开的那种材料
words.recall_hint: al-（朝）+ loy（绑）→ 两种金属绑成一体

words.root_logic: a-（ad- 朝）+ vail（值、有力）→ 顶得上用 → 有助于
words.origin: 中古英语 availen，由 a-（拉丁 ad 向）＋古法语 vail-（valoir 值）← 拉丁语 valere（有力、值）
words.native_definition: to be of use or help; to make use of something
words.core_concept: whether the thing turns out to carry any weight – 那东西到底顶不顶得上用
words.core_image: 带来的工具往锁上一试，居然真能拧开
examples: Nothing availed against the storm.
She availed herself of the offer.
semantic_expansions: 有助于/效用：那东西顶得上用、有分量
利用：把这份分量拿来用在自己身上
words.recall_hint: a-（朝）+ vail（值、有力）→ 顶得上用

words.root_logic: bene（好）+ gn（gen 出身、天性）→ 天性好的 → 和善、良性
words.origin: 古法语 benigne ← 拉丁语 benignus（善良的）← bene（好）＋genus（出身、种）
words.native_definition: kind and gentle; not dangerous in nature
words.core_concept: born with a mild nature, so it does no harm – 生来性子温的，因此不伤人
words.core_image: 护士说话放轻，动作也慢，针扎下去几乎没觉出
examples: He gave a benign smile.
The tumour turned out to be benign.
semantic_expansions: 和善的/温和的：生来性子温、不伤人
良性的：同一份「天性不凶」用在病灶上
words.recall_hint: bene（好）+ gn（出身天性）→ 生来性子温的

words.root_logic: caedere（切、砍）→ caementum（砍碎的石屑）→ 碎石烧成的胶结料
words.origin: 古法语 ciment ← 拉丁语 caementum（采石场砍下的碎石）← caedere（切、砍）
words.native_definition: a grey powder that hardens when mixed with water, used in building
words.core_concept: the stone chips ground down and made to bind again – 砍碎的石头磨成粉，又让它重新黏合
words.core_image: 灰粉兑水搅成糊，抹进砖缝，第二天硬得抠不动
examples: They mixed cement and sand.
The talks cemented their friendship.
semantic_expansions: 水泥/胶结剂：砍碎的石屑磨粉后重新黏合之物
黏合：把两边像水泥那样固牢
words.recall_hint: caedere（切砍）→ caementum（碎石屑）→ 烧成胶结料
